answer.generated: The error-correcting output code (ECOC) method simplifies the classification task by decomposing the original complex classification problem into a series of simpler subtasks. Each subtask focuses on distinguishing between a specific class and all others, rather than attempting to classify the entire dataset in one step. This approach makes the problem more tractable, often leading to improved predictive performance because it allows the use of simpler base learners for each subtask, which can be more effectively optimized. By solving these simpler subproblems, ECOC then combines their outputs to make the final prediction, thereby enhancing overall accuracy and robustness of the classifier.
